title: Kinds of Moon Bridge
summary: Safe, Attack and Wild bridges between caerns.

claims.text: A Safe Moon Bridge links two caerns with the consent of both Gatekeepers and both totems, and the Rite of the Opened Bridge can make it safer still.
An Attack Moon Bridge is forced to a caern that does not want it, breaking through its totem’s defences with the Rite of Luna’s Spear; it is very dangerous to travel until established.
A Wild Moon Bridge is the third kind, opened without the usual control.
How far a bridge can reach depends on caern rank, from about 1,000 miles for the lowest to 10,000 for the greatest.

title: The Sept of the Tri-Spiral
summary: A Fianna caern in Ireland with three centres.

claims.text: Brugh na Boinne in County Meath is a level 5 Gnosis, Honour and Plenty caern under the Stag and Dana, open to all but controlled by the Fianna.
No other known caern has three centres: the passage-grave mounds of Newgrange, Knowth and Dowth, set in a triangle a kilometre on each side.
Fianna Kinfolk farm the land around it, and the sept’s leaders all take the surname MacFionn and pass the property to their successors.

title: The Smiling Happy Buddha
summary: A totem of Respect, Background cost 5.

claims.text: The Smiling Happy Buddha, also called Mi-lo Fo, the Laughing Buddha, grants followers tranquil peace and provides for their material needs; this totem is patron of silver- and goldsmiths.
Packs chosen by the totem gain two extra Willpower points and three points of liquid Resources each story.
In times of great stress the totem may appear to help renowned Garou focus their will, much like the Silver Fang Gift Mindblock.

title: Katajuta
summary: An Uktena caern in the Australian Outback.

claims.text: The caern’s bawn is vast, over 400 miles by 200, because so few people and Garou live there and food must be sought over great distances; Uktena scouts always patrol its edges.

Its centre, the Glade of the Ancestors, is a pool among ghost gum and bloodbark trees, which the sept holds to be the past lives of many of its members; in times of great threat the trees are said to bleed red sap.
Diving through the pool leads to the Dreaming Womb, a cave of painted symbols where the barrier to the Umbra is thinnest; if the paintings are not kept fresh the caern loses power.

title: Kitsune
summary: The fox shapeshifters and their Jyu-ho.

claims.text: A Kitsune with more than one tail ages one year for every span of years equal to its tails, and age makes the Nine-Tails stronger and more beautiful rather than weaker.
A Fox needs more than five tails to count as an elder, and many never become one however long they live.
Kitsune dislike crude violence, most master their Rage through Zen practice or mantras, and some learn to wield a blade in the mouth in fox form.
Their Gifts, called Jyu-ho, use Gnosis or Rage; each path borrows Garou Gifts of a matching auspice, such as Doshi with Theurge Gifts and Eji with Ahroun Gifts.
